pr_title: Bluetooth: Host: Allow setting more than 251 bytes of adv data
pr_body:
When the application sets more than 251 bytes of advertising data,
the data is sent over multiple HCI commands.
This is only allowed if the advertiser is not running
as defined by the HCI specification.

The data is sent to the controller one AD-field at the time.
If an AD-field is larger than BT_HCI_LE_EXT_ADV_FRAG_MAX_LEN,
the data is split over two commands.
This introduces some additional complexity.

Fixes: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/37367

Signed-off-by: Rubin Gerritsen <rubin.gerritsen@nordicsemi.no>
pr_comments: @rugeGerritsen can you address the review comments?
Rebased on main. No changes introduced

issue_context.title: Bluetooth: Host: Support setting long advertising data
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
I want to be able to transmit 1650 bytes of advertising data using a single advertiser as supported by a given Bluetooth Controller. Currently the host only supports setting advertising data in one operation. Therefore the maximum advertising and periodic advertising data length is limited to 251 bytes.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
- If the advertising data is longer than 251 bytes, the host shall set the advertising data in multiple steps using the parameter named `operation` in the commands:
  - HCI LE Set Extended Advertising Data (Core_v5.3, Vol 4, Part E, Section 7.8.54)
  - HCI LE Set Extended Scan Response Data (Core_v5.3, Vol 4, Part E, Section 7.8.55)
  - HCI LE Set Periodic Advertising Data (Core_v5.3, Vol 4, Part E, Section 7.8.62)
- Setting more than 251 bytes while advertising shall return an error code as it is not allowed by HCI.
comments: @rugeGerritsen Add the Fixes with this issue number in the PR so that this issue gets linked and gets closed when the PR is merged.

```suggestion
static int hci_set_ad_ext(const struct bt_le_ext_adv *adv, uint16_t hci_op,
```

Had to check this up. Maybe we should rename this to ADV_FRAG_MINIMIZE?
Looks strange to disable fragmentation when we are fragmenting the commands.
Yes, I agree, this define may be renamed. Do you want me to change it in this PR?
hci.h is semi-public, I think a comment should be enough.
I'm wondering if it would be better to use the `net_buf_simple` API to continuously add data to a buffer like this; that way you can avoid keeping track of `offset` yourself.
I gave it a try, the code did not become more readable in my opinion as I anyways had to access its length field

```suggestion
static int hci_set_adv_ext_fragmented(const struct bt_le_ext_adv *adv, uint16_t hci_op,
```
The scope of these variables can be smaller if moved to the loops.

This could potentially be a lot of commands. But I guess the tradeoff would be complexity in the code vs effeciency in the HCI commands. Have you checked the processing of this if you had to do this over UART for example?
I'm hoping RPMsg is not too bad, or combined build for that matter.

I did not consider performance being a big issue here. Setting long advertising data is typically done once or very seldom.
If performance is an issue, I agree that we could use the non-sync variant of sending commands to the controller, but that makes error handling more difficult.

Fair enough. Just curious, but if performance becomes an issue this can be rewritten to be send less HCI commands.
No not caching the error is just trouble, send_sync is preferred.

Here and in lines 462 and 463 you use the value 2, which is of course the size of the len and type parameters, but this may not be obvious for other. Do we have any `#define` for that? Else I suggest storing that in `const` variable and calculate by `sizeof(len)` and `sizeof(type)`.
